strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across five diverse subsurface benchmarks with consistent performance improvements over multiple baselines (U-Net, FNO, MGN, MGN-LSTM)
Well-motivated architecture addressing real limitations of existing approaches (mesh restriction in CNNs, limited long-range dependencies in GNNs, mesh flexibility issues in FNOs)
Strong empirical results including significant computational speedups (4902× over GEOS, 1.8× over MGN-LSTM on pressure) with practical significance for energy sector applications
Good reproducibility with extensive implementation details, hyperparameters, dataset descriptions, and training procedures provided in appendices
Effective presentation with clear visualizations and well-organized narrative that clearly communicates technical contributions and experimental setup
Practical capability to learn directly from adaptive mesh optimization (DMO) simulations, enabling mesh-agnostic predictions across different grid types
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty—combines existing components (perceiver encoder, standard GNO, simple gating) with main contribution being engineering integration rather than conceptual innovation; gated fusion mechanism (Eq. 1) lacks justification over alternative designs

Overstated super-resolution and mesh-convergence claims: on heterogeneous ATES data shows significant degradation at full resolution; paper acknowledges performance 'ultimately bounded by mesh convergence' but framing suggests broader capability

Insufficient out-of-distribution evaluation: Section 4.2 tests on same geological structures with different random seeds rather than fundamentally different regimes, scales, or physics; 'robust generalization' claim is overstated

Critical ablation studies missing: no ablation on gating function or perceiver depth; no systematic analysis of when local vs global information dominates; no component contribution analysis despite Table 1 showing small improvements from individual components
Incomplete baseline comparisons: CarBench results from Ehrefaie et al. (2025) under different training setup; no sampling script provided; missing comparisons with recent mesh-agnostic methods
Scalability concerns inadequately addressed: memory requirements up to 231.8 GB (Table 7), 55-minute training epochs; memory-computation tradeoffs not discussed; unclear scaling to larger systems

Limited theoretical justification for design choices and no systematic analysis of failure modes; higher errors at fault zones (Figure 3) noted but not discussed; unclear why heterogeneous meshes show larger degradation than smooth aerodynamic data

strengths: Novel fused global-local attention mechanism that effectively balances long-range pressure propagation with local conservation constraints, appearing to be the first such combination in neural operator literature

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 diverse subsurface benchmarks (CO2 storage, hydrocarbon extraction, aquifer thermal storage, wastewater injection) with multiple evaluation metrics, demonstrating broad applicability

Impressive cross-dataset generalization results (Table 6: 86.7% R² when trained on Channelized data with limited labels vs 32% for supervised baseline), showing practical utility for transfer learning in subsurface modeling
Mesh-agnostic learning capability—APT learns directly from adaptive mesh simulations without interpolation to fixed grids, a genuine technical advance over prior methods

Exceptional reproducibility documentation including detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, training costs, and dataset descriptions in appendices; achieves 4902× speedup over GEOS simulator
Strong ablation studies and analysis sections (Tables 1, 4, 6, 14) clearly demonstrating the importance of each architectural component, particularly the fused attention mechanism
Well-organized presentation with clear mathematical formulations, high-quality visualizations, and rigorous problem setup; addresses important practical application in energy and climate domains
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging mesh convergence bounds and performance degradation at full resolution, without overstating contributions
weaknesses: Super-resolution claims are somewhat overstated: Table 3 shows APT degrades to 1.8% error at full resolution vs 0.01% on coarse grids; paper lacks architectural explanation for why a mesh-invariant model should degrade at higher query resolution

Computational speedup comparison with GEOS (Table 10) compares single-core CPU full physics simulation to GPU neural inference—while useful, this unfair hardware comparison needs clearer contextualization
Mesh convergence behavior unexplained: Section 4.1 claims performance improves 0.5% with higher query resolution but provides no theoretical or architectural justification for this observation
Limited comparison to physics-based baselines: most comparisons are against ML methods (U-Net, FNO, MGN-LSTM); evaluation against advanced numerical solvers beyond GEOS would strengthen claims
No real-world validation: all evaluation uses synthetic simulation data; validation against actual field measurements would significantly strengthen practical impact claims

Originality primarily in combination: while the fused attention mechanism is novel, individual components (Perceivers, GNOs, Transformers) are established; the contribution is more incremental than foundational
Generalization demonstrated only within subsurface domain; broader applicability to other PDE-governed systems remains undemonstrated
Missing ablation details: Table 1 shows comparisons without accounting for parameter count differences (APT 1.36M vs FNO 1.48M); saturation improvement over U-FNO is modest (1.8× vs 1.1×)
Uncertainty quantification absent: no error bars or confidence bounds on predictions, limiting assessment of prediction reliability for practical deployment
Code release promised but no repository URL or timeline specified; reproducibility depends on availability of external simulators (GEOS, IC-FERST)

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across 7 diverse subsurface benchmarks including irregular and adaptive meshes, demonstrating robust generalization
Practical impact: 6,800× speedup over numerical simulators while maintaining high accuracy, enabling real-time decision-making for subsurface applications
First architecture to learn directly from HR-adaptive mesh refinement (DMO) simulations without interpolation, preserving sharp physical fronts
Clear ablation studies (Table 1) systematically validate the fused local-global design choice
Novel cross-dataset training capability (Table 6: 32%→86.7% R² improvement) enabling foundation model potential despite incompatible mesh topologies
Mesh-agnostic design addresses real practitioner challenges with heterogeneous geological discretizations
Extensive reproducibility details with hyperparameters, training efficiency metrics, and promised code release
Handles multiple physics types (multiphase flow, heat transport, compositional flow) across scales from 1k to 1M cells
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core components (Perceiver, GNO, gated fusion) are established; contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation. Gated fusion mechanism (Eq. 1) is straightforward element-wise weighting with insufficient justification for this design over alternatives

Overstated super-resolution claims: on heterogeneous ATES data (realistic subsurface), APT degrades 1.8% at full resolution; paper correctly attributes this to training data fidelity but abstract claims mislead about architectural capability

Modest improvements on key benchmarks: hydrocarbon saturation error 0.32% vs U-FNO 0.66% (unclear if significant), OOD generalization only 0.5% R² improvement, ranks 7/12 on CarBench; basin-scale pressure error 0.56% is worse than Nested FNO's 0.47%

Insufficient technical justification: element-wise gating not compared to alternatives; how G is learned (per-location vs shared) unclear; no ablation on latent token counts or input sampling sensitivity; counterintuitive that 'local-only' matches 'fused' performance on some metrics

Missing critical analysis: no quantification of what physical phenomena model learns; no uncertainty quantification (critical for practitioner decisions); limited failure mode discussion; transfer to fundamentally new domains not demonstrated (only tested on distribution variations)

Experimental concerns: CarBench evaluation uses unofficial implementation affecting reproducibility; error bars inconsistently provided; random seeds not specified; cross-dataset training only combines two LGR datasets with similar physics

Presentation issues: title incorrectly labels GNO as 'attention'; notation inconsistencies (G† vs Gθ); key baseline details relegated to appendix; Figure 3 error maps difficult to interpret; multiple heterogeneous metrics (R², L2, plume error, pressure error) complicate comparison

Limited theoretical insight: no formal justification for why fused approach is optimal; missing analysis of gate learning dynamics; positional encoding strategy not justified; how anchor supernodes selected for ATES described vaguely

strengths: Novel capability to learn directly from HR-adaptive mesh refinement simulations without interpolation—a genuinely new contribution with significant practical value for subsurface applications
Well-motivated architecture combining global Perceiver encoder with local GNO encoder; fused design clearly justified for capturing both long-range pressure propagation and sharp saturation fronts
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across five diverse benchmarks with extensive baseline comparisons (9+ methods) and thorough ablation studies demonstrating the value of fusion
Strong practical results: 6,800× speedup over ECLIPSE simulator; 1.8-3.75× improvements on faulted CO2 storage; 97% parameter reduction vs Nested FNO while maintaining accuracy

Rigorous and honest treatment of limitations: authors appropriately acknowledge super-resolution limitations tied to training data, scaling demonstrated only on single physics type, and CarBench experimental setup differences
Extensive reproducibility documentation with detailed implementation specifics, training costs, and dataset descriptions in appendices enabling verification and future work
Enables cross-dataset learning despite different mesh topologies, a capability previously impossible with fixed-mesh methods—significant for foundation model development
weaknesses: Moderate architectural novelty: main contribution combines existing techniques (Perceiver, GNO, gated fusion); limited theoretical justification for why this specific combination is optimal; simple gating mechanism (Eq. 1) not thoroughly motivated against alternatives

CarBench results undermine SOTA claims: APT achieves 96.0% R² vs AB-UPT's 96.75%; authors attribute gap to experimental setup differences rather than method, which weakens reproducibility and generality claims

Super-resolution evaluation inconclusive: 1.8% degradation on ATES at full resolution, with justification that training data limits performance rather than architecture; 0.5% CarBench improvement marginal given experimental variability; practical super-resolution benefit unclear

Foundation model positioning premature: scaling behavior (Table 7) demonstrated only on single ATES physics type; authors explicitly acknowledge this limitation; cross-dataset learning tested only on related CO2 storage datasets, not fundamentally different domains

Non-SOTA performance on general PDE benchmarks (Table 17): second-best on 2 of 3 tasks, behind Transolver; undermines generality claims and suggests specialized subsurface design may not transfer well

Evaluation methodology concerns: APT trained with direct one-step prediction while baselines rolled out autoregressively; different modeling assumptions complicate direct comparisons; no analysis of rollout error accumulation over extended horizons

Incomplete design justification: limited ablations on architectural choices (why Perceiver vs alternatives? sensitivity to supernode count? radius graph pooling sensitivity?); feature analysis or attention visualizations missing

Presentation and organization: key results scattered across 31-page appendices; CarBench results (Table 14) and implementation details relegated to appendices; should be more prominent given claimed contributions
